topics.title: Underwriting and underwriting commission
topics.summary: What underwriting is, its kinds, marked and unmarked applications, and the commission allowed by law.
notes: Underwriting is an agreement under which the underwriter undertakes to take up the shares or debentures not subscribed by the public, in return for a commission.

Complete underwriting covers the whole issue; partial underwriting covers part of it; firm underwriting means the underwriter also applies for a fixed number of shares regardless of public subscription.
Marked applications carry the stamp of a particular underwriter and are credited to that underwriter; unmarked applications are shared among underwriters in the ratio of their gross liability.

Under the Companies Act, 2013 (section 40) and its rules, underwriting commission may not exceed 5% of the issue price of shares or 2.5% of the issue price of debentures, or the rate authorised by the articles, whichever is less.
outcomes: Compute each underwriter's net liability with marked and unmarked applications
Calculate underwriting commission and pass the journal entries

topics.title: Methods of valuing goodwill
topics.summary: Average profit, super profit, capitalisation and annuity methods.
notes: Goodwill is the value of a firm's reputation and its ability to earn more than normal profits; it is an intangible asset.
Average profit method: Goodwill = Average maintainable profit × Number of years' purchase.
Super profit method: Normal profit = Capital employed × Normal rate of return ÷ 100; Super profit = Average maintainable profit − Normal profit; Goodwill = Super profit × Number of years' purchase.
Capitalisation of average profit: Capitalised value = Average profit × 100 ÷ Normal rate of return; Goodwill = Capitalised value − Net assets (capital employed).
Capitalisation of super profit: Goodwill = Super profit × 100 ÷ Normal rate of return.
Annuity method: Goodwill = Super profit × present value of an annuity of ₹1 for the given years at the given rate.
outcomes: Value goodwill by the average profit, super profit and capitalisation methods
Adjust past profits to find maintainable profit

topics.title: Net assets, yield and fair value methods
topics.summary: Intrinsic (net assets) value, yield value and fair value of equity shares.
notes: Net assets (intrinsic value) method: Value per equity share = Net assets available to equity shareholders ÷ Number of equity shares.

Net assets available to equity shareholders = Total assets at realisable value (including goodwill) − Outside liabilities − Preference share capital (and any preference dividend in arrears where applicable).
Yield method: Value per share = (Expected rate of return ÷ Normal rate of return) × Paid-up value per share.
Fair value = (Intrinsic value + Yield value) ÷ 2.
outcomes: Value equity shares by the net assets and yield methods
Find the fair value of a share

topics.title: Schedule III formats
topics.summary: Preparing the statement of profit and loss and the balance sheet in the Schedule III format.
notes: Company financial statements follow Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013.
The balance sheet has two parts: Equity and Liabilities (shareholders' funds, non-current liabilities, current liabilities) and Assets (non-current assets, current assets).
Details are given in notes to accounts, which are referred to by number on the face of the statements.
outcomes: Prepare a company's statement of profit and loss and balance sheet with notes

chapters.title: Introduction to Cost Accounting and the Cost Sheet

topics.title: Stock levels and EOQ
topics.summary: Economic order quantity and the reorder, minimum and maximum stock levels.
notes: Economic order quantity: EOQ = √(2AO ÷ C), where A is annual consumption in units, O the cost of placing one order and C the carrying cost per unit per year.
Reorder level = Maximum consumption × Maximum reorder period.
Minimum level = Reorder level − (Normal consumption × Normal reorder period).
Maximum level = Reorder level + Reorder quantity − (Minimum consumption × Minimum reorder period).
Average stock level = (Minimum level + Maximum level) ÷ 2, or Minimum level + ½ Reorder quantity.

topics.title: Incentive plans
topics.summary: Time rate, piece rate and the Halsey and Rowan premium plans.
notes: Time saved = Time allowed − Time taken.
Halsey plan: Bonus = 50% × Time saved × Rate per hour; Earnings = Time taken × Rate + Bonus.
Rowan plan: Bonus = (Time taken ÷ Time allowed) × Time saved × Rate per hour; Earnings = Time taken × Rate + Bonus.
outcomes: Compute earnings under Halsey and Rowan plans

topics.title: Marginal costing and break-even analysis
topics.summary: Contribution, P/V ratio, break-even point and margin of safety.
notes: Contribution = Sales − Variable cost.
P/V ratio = Contribution ÷ Sales × 100.
Break-even point (units) = Fixed cost ÷ Contribution per unit; break-even sales (₹) = Fixed cost ÷ P/V ratio.
Margin of safety = Actual sales − Break-even sales; also Profit ÷ P/V ratio.
outcomes: Find the break-even point and margin of safety
